solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

indicators.note: one word standing outside another wraps around it, so the second sits within the first

parts.note: to confront is to face
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A man called Jack is challenged as he stands beside his car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jack' looks like a man's name but is the playing card; 'perhaps' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A jack is one of the picture cards in a pack, along with king and queen, so it is an example of a face card.

indicators.note: to conceal is to keep something inside out of sight, so the letters lie within the words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A surly actor is keeping the truth to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A fact is something known to be true, a piece of truth.

indicators.note: hugging something means wrapping arms around it, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: to confer is to discuss
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: An instruction to talk about hugging a tree.
explanation.definitionFit: A conifer is a cone-bearing evergreen tree, such as a pine or fir.

clue.text: Debate County spurning United but welcoming Rovers

indicators.note: welcoming a guest means taking them in, so one word goes inside the other
spurning something is rejecting it, so that letter is thrown out

parts.note: taken as written
U is the abbreviation for United, as in football club names
taken as written

explanation.surface: A football argument: County snub United but invite Rovers, all common British club names.
explanation.walkthrough: County, United and Rovers are all common parts of English football club names, which makes the surface read as a transfer squabble.
explanation.definitionFit: A controversy is a prolonged public dispute, a debate argued over by opposing sides.

indicators.note: reportedly means as told by word of mouth, so it is the sound that counts

parts.note: a wrapper is a cover; the W is silent

explanation.surface: Word is that someone will do a cover version of an Eminem song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cover' suggests a cover version of a song; here it is a wrapping.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminem is an American hip-hop artist, so an example of a rapper; 'say' marks the example.

clue.text: Superstar not doing anything on the radio

indicators.note: what is heard on the radio is only sound, so the word is chosen by how it is said

parts.note: someone not doing anything is idle

explanation.surface: A celebrity DJ sits about doing nothing during a broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: An idol is a hugely admired star, a person worshipped by fans.

parts.note: a tie in a match is a draw

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of the word is kept

parts.note: the final letter of gown

explanation.surface: A drawing of a tie and a gown at the end of a fashion sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tie' looks like the neckwear beside the gown, but it is a drawn game.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawn is the past participle of draw, so it means sketched with a pencil.

clue.text: Freedom quietly dropped from trite remark

indicators.note: something dropped from a word is let fall out of it, leaving the rest behind

parts.note: a platitude is a trite, overused remark
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly

explanation.surface: A dull comment is quietly cut from a speech about freedom.
explanation.definitionFit: Latitude means scope or leeway to act as one chooses, a kind of liberty.

indicators.note: to embrace is to hold in one's arms, so one word holds the other inside it

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prison inmate
taken as written

explanation.surface: A prisoner hugs the clergyman who visits the jail.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a member of the clergy attached to a cathedral, so a priest.

clue.text: Nice to bypass large farm labourer

indicators.note: bypassing something means going around without stopping there, so that letter is skipped

parts.note: nice means agreeable, pleasing
L is the abbreviation for large, as on clothing sizes

explanation.surface: It would be nice to avoid a large farm, says a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: PLEASANT loses its L. 'Nice' looks like the French city but is just the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a poor agricultural worker who works the land.

definitions.note: a noun here, the military as a body

indicators.note: bananas is slang for crazy, so these letters go wild into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Soldiers yelled for bananas at mealtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bananas' looks like the fruit being demanded, but it is slang for mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The armed forces are a nation's army, navy and air force, the military collectively.

clue.text: Counterfeit guys enthralled by child's flower

parts.note: to forge is to counterfeit

indicators.note: something enthralled is held captive, so it sits inside what holds it

parts.note: a tot is a small child
guys are men

explanation.surface: A child's flower turns out to be fake, made by some men.
explanation.definitionFit: The forget-me-not is a small blue-flowered plant of the genus Myosotis.

clue.text: Tiny piece of relic apt for redevelopment

indicators.note: something marked for redevelopment is to be rebuilt in a different form

parts.note: the letters as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A small fragment of an old relic is suitable for a new building scheme.
explanation.definitionFit: A particle is a minute portion or speck of matter.

clue.text: Show up in a river swimming

indicators.note: something swimming is moving about loosely, so these letters are set in motion into a new order

parts.note: the letters as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone turns up by swimming down a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrive is to turn up or appear at a place.

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party or celebration
red is wine; 'with' just adds it on

explanation.surface: Someone loved a party that served wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Adored is a stronger synonym of loved, meaning cherished deeply.

clue.text: Some of dinner is Ottoman rice dish

indicators.note: some of means only part of, so the letters are a run taken from within the words

parts.note: the letters run across all three words

explanation.surface: Part of the dinner is an Ottoman rice dish, perhaps a pilaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ottoman rice dish' suggests pilaf; the dish is Italian.
explanation.definitionFit: Risotto is an Italian dish of rice cooked slowly in stock.

clue.text: Struggle ninja regularly avoided in capital city

parts.note: to vie is to struggle or compete

indicators.note: regularly avoided means every other letter is skipped, keeping the alternate ones

parts.note: the first, third and fifth letters of ninja

explanation.surface: A fight with a ninja is dodged in a capital.
explanation.definitionFit: Vienna is the capital of Austria.

indicators.note: something ruined is wrecked, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the letters as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Another artist has spoilt a BBC programme.
explanation.definitionFit: The Traitors is a BBC reality game show in which contestants hunt for hidden betrayers among them.

indicators.note: overlooking the leader means ignoring the front, so the first letter is left out

parts.note: terror is great fear

explanation.surface: Fear that the leader is ignoring a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: TERROR loses its first letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: An error is a blunder or slip, a synonym for a mistake.

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a hut is a small cabin

explanation.walkthrough: 'Close' looks like the adjective near, as in a cabin close by, but it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To shut a door is to close it; the words are synonyms as verbs.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a commotion or palaver, a noun
second meaning: a bag small enough to take aboard a plane

explanation.surface: A traveller makes a scene about their cabin bag.
explanation.definitionFit: A carry-on is British slang for a fuss, and also the bag a passenger takes into an aircraft cabin.

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to hear or perceive, as in a remark
second meaning: a snag concealed in a deal

explanation.surface: Someone works out that there is a hidden drawback.
explanation.definitionFit: To catch what someone says is to make it out, and a catch is a concealed snag in an offer.

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: ahead of schedule means early

explanation.surface: A nobleman turns up nearly ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British peer ranking below a marquess and above a viscount.

parts.note: to pass is to go on or proceed
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: An instruction to go to the left to collect your travel papers.
explanation.definitionFit: A passport is the official identity document needed to cross borders.
